note: Part 12 (L = SCC-180). The banner printed `git reset --hard origin/$1` as its remedy and an agent ran it in the MAIN checkout, destroying three sessions' uncommitted work. There is no git hook for `reset`; the only fix is to stop printing it. The plan's third declared mutant - drop the DIRTY fixture - is not mutable as a one-string swap (it is a whole `with` block), so RH-B2's anti-vacuity is held by RH-B1 re-advancing HEAD before it, and by L-3 below which proves the two cases are not the same assertion.

mutants.why: restore `--hard` in the banner - the shipped defect, exactly as it read on 2026-08-15
mutants.original: git reset --keep origin/$1            # ONLY if this lane was already pushed
mutants.mutated: git reset --hard origin/$1            # ONLY if this lane was already pushed

mutants.why: delete the imperative-vs-prose distinction. `payload` stops stripping `echo "`, so the detector goes BLIND to printed command lines - and RH1 ("no imperatives found") is exactly what a blind detector reports, so it stays green. This mutant is why RH1b exists: the sweep found the block certifying a check that could no longer fail.

the DIRTY case is not a restatement of the CLEAN one. Force `--keep` to `--hard` in the drill itself: the clean rewind is unchanged (RH-B1 still passes) and the dirty tree is silently destroyed, which is the whole incident.
